title: Exact values of the six trig functions
summary: Combine reference angles and quadrant signs with the special-angle table to find exact values without a calculator.
objectives: Recall the exact sine, cosine and tangent of 30°, 45° and 60°
Use the quadrant to choose the sign
Find csc, sec and cot exactly and rationalize

lesson.md:
# Exact values of the six trig functions

A calculator says $\cos 210^\circ\approx-0.866$. The exam wants $-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Every exact value comes from the same three-step routine: **find the reference angle, read its value from the special-angle table, then choose the sign from the quadrant**.

lesson.title: The six functions on the unit circle
lesson.md: If the terminal side of $\theta$ meets the unit circle at $(x,y)$, then $\cos\theta=x$, $\sin\theta=y$ and $\tan\theta=\dfrac{y}{x}$. The other three are their reciprocals, $\csc\theta=\dfrac1y$, $\sec\theta=\dfrac1x$ and $\cot\theta=\dfrac{x}{y}$, always written after rationalizing.

lesson.question: Without a calculator: what is the sign of $\cos 210^\circ$?

options.why: Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, and $x>0$ only in Quadrants I and IV.
$210^\circ$ is in Quadrant III, where every point has $x<0$.
Cosine is zero only at $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$.

lesson.explanation: Keep this in mind: the sign comes from the quadrant, never from the reference angle.

lesson.md:
## The special-angle table

These rows are worth memorizing. Every other exact value on the exam is built from them with a reference angle and a sign.

lesson.title: A pattern that helps
lesson.md: The sines of $0^\circ, 30^\circ, 45^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ$ are $\frac{\sqrt0}{2}, \frac{\sqrt1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt2}{2}, \frac{\sqrt3}{2}, \frac{\sqrt4}{2}$. The cosines are the same list backwards. Tangent is sine over cosine, written after rationalizing: $\tan30^\circ=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt3}{3}$.

## Reference angles and quadrant signs

The table only covers Quadrant I. For any other angle, use reference angles and quadrant signs together: the **reference angle** gives the size of the answer and the **quadrant** gives its sign. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate and sine is the $y$-coordinate, so the sign only asks which side of each axis the point is on.

lesson.title: $210^\circ$ on the unit circle
lesson.caption: The reference angle is $30^\circ$; in Quadrant III both coordinates are negative.
Signs by quadrant: “All Students Take Calculus”

lesson.md:
## Putting it together

Every exact value is a size times a sign. Find them separately, then put them together: first the quadrant, then the reference angle, then the table, and only at the end the sign.

steps.md: **Quadrant.** $180^\circ<210^\circ<270^\circ$, so the terminal side is in Quadrant III.
**Sign.** Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, negative in Quadrant III: $\cos210^\circ=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
steps.note: The size comes from the reference angle; the sign comes from the quadrant. Never take the sign from the table.

lesson.title: The exact-value routine
lesson.caption: First make the angle coterminal in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$. Size and sign are found separately, then put together.

lesson.md: Taking the sign from the reference angle. $\cos30^\circ$ is positive, but $\cos210^\circ$ is not: the answer $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ has the right size and the wrong sign.

lesson.intro: A student found $\tan 300^\circ$. Which line is wrong?
lines: Tangent is positive in Quadrant IV, so $\tan300^\circ=\sqrt3$.

lesson.md:
## The reciprocal functions

For $\csc$, $\sec$ and $\cot$, find the matching sine, cosine or tangent first, flip it and rationalize the denominator. A reciprocal keeps the sign, and the reciprocal of $0$ does not exist: $\csc180^\circ$ and $\sec90^\circ$ are **undefined**.

points: Size from the **reference angle**, sign from the **quadrant**.
Memorize the $30^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ rows; the cosines are the sines backwards.
All Students Take Calculus: which functions are positive in Quadrants I, II, III and IV.
Reciprocals keep the sign, and $\frac10$ is undefined.

hints: $150^\circ$ is in Quadrant II with reference angle $30^\circ$.

wrongs.why: $150^\circ$ is in Quadrant II, where sine (the $y$-coordinate) is positive.
For a $30^\circ$ reference angle, sine goes with $\frac12$; $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ is the cosine.

solution.md: $\tan225^\circ=\tan45^\circ=1$: in Quadrant III sine and cosine are both negative, so their ratio is positive.

wrongs.why: In Quadrant III sine and cosine are both negative, so tangent (their ratio) is positive.

solution.md: $240^\circ$ is in Quadrant III with reference angle $60^\circ$, so $\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}=-\sin60^\circ=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

wrongs.why: Right size, wrong sign: $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ is in Quadrant III, where sine is negative.
That is $\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}$. For a $60^\circ$ reference angle, sine goes with $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

options.why: Quadrant IV, reference angle $60^\circ$, and cosine is positive there.
Cosine is positive in Quadrant IV, so there is no minus sign.
The reference angle of $300^\circ$ is $60^\circ$, not $30^\circ$.

hints: Find the quadrant and the reference angle.
In which quadrant is $210^\circ$? What is its reference angle?
$\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Now the sign: is $x$ positive or negative in Quadrant III?

solution.md: $210^\circ$ is in Quadrant III with reference angle $30^\circ$. Cosine is negative there, so $\cos210^\circ=-\cos30^\circ=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

wrongs.why: Right size, wrong sign. $210^\circ$ is in Quadrant III, where every point of the unit circle has a negative $x$-coordinate, and cosine is that $x$: $\cos210^\circ=-\cos30^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
That is $\sin210^\circ$. For a $30^\circ$ reference angle, cosine goes with $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and sine with $\frac12$.
That is $\cos60^\circ$, and positive. The reference angle of $210^\circ$ is $30^\circ$ and cosine is negative in Quadrant III.

prompt.md: Find the exact value of $\csc 180^\circ$. If it does not exist, write “undefined”.

solution.md: $\sin180^\circ=0$, and $\frac10$ does not exist, so $\csc180^\circ$ is **undefined**.

wrongs.why: That is $\sin180^\circ$ itself; its reciprocal cannot be $0$ (no number has reciprocal $0$). Since $\sin180^\circ=0$, $\csc180^\circ=\frac10$ is undefined.
Right size, wrong sign: cosine, and so secant, is negative in Quadrant II.
That is $\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}$. Secant is its reciprocal.
That is $\tan330^\circ$. Cotangent is its reciprocal: $-\sqrt3$.

prompt.md: Find all angles $\theta$ in $[0^\circ, 360^\circ)$ with $\sin\theta=-\dfrac12$. Separate them with commas.

hints: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV.

solution.md: Reference angle $30^\circ$; Quadrant III gives $210^\circ$ and Quadrant IV gives $330^\circ$.

wrongs.why: Those angles have $\sin\theta=+\frac12$. A negative sine needs Quadrants III and IV.
Give angles between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$: $-30^\circ$ is coterminal with $330^\circ$.

hints: Find each of the four values first.

solution.md: True: at $90^\circ$ the point is $(0,1)$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{y}{x}=\frac10$.

prompt.md: Match each expression with its exact value.

solution.md: In Quadrant III sine and cosine are negative and tangent is positive; $\csc240^\circ=-\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=-\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}$.

cards.front: In which quadrants is cosine negative?
All Students Take Calculus: {{c1::all}} are positive in QI, {{c2::sine}} in QII, {{c3::tangent}} in QIII and {{c4::cosine}} in QIV.

mistakes.title: Sign taken from the table
mistakes.why: The table gives the size for the reference angle; the quadrant gives the sign.

mistakes.title: Sine and cosine swapped
mistakes.why: At $30^\circ$ the point is low on the circle: its height (sine) is the small value $\frac12$.
